questions.stem: In the data product ecosystem, where does the journey of every data product start?
options: In the Data Preparation Zone, where raw, fragmented inputs are collected, validated and modelled for reuse
In the OLAP Zone, where dashboards are built
In the sandbox of a data scientist
questions.explanation: Every data product starts in the Data Preparation Zone, which lays the architectural backbone by collecting, validating and modelling raw inputs for reuse.

questions.stem: Which modelling approach in the Data Preparation Zone is described as designed for agility, historisation and traceability in complex data landscapes?
questions.explanation: Data Vault Modelling is the approach designed for agility, historisation and traceability in complex data landscapes.

questions.stem: What are Ensemble Techniques such as Focal Point and Anchor used for in the Data Preparation Zone?
options: Exposing data externally as a service
questions.explanation: Ensemble techniques such as Focal Point and Anchor are used to unify fragmented entities across domains.

questions.stem: Which of the following is NOT listed as a key component of the OLAP Zone?
questions.explanation: The OLAP Zone comprises Data Marts, Semantic Layers, Inference Tables and Sandboxes; Feature Store Design belongs to the Data Preparation Zone.

questions.stem: What do semantic layers in the OLAP Zone do?
options: Historise every change to a record
Replace the need for data stewards
Translate physical schemas into business-friendly views, empowering self-service without SQL knowledge
questions.explanation: Semantic layers translate physical schemas into business-friendly views so that users can self-serve without needing SQL.

questions.stem: Which of the following is given as an example of a Data-As-a-Product (DAaP) asset?
options: Curated customer profile datasets used across marketing, support and analytics
A one-off spreadsheet emailed to a manager
A sandbox used for a single experiment
A raw log file from a web server
questions.explanation: DAaP examples include curated customer profile datasets used across marketing, support and analytics, governed KPI APIs and shared ML features.

options: A modelling technique for data warehouses
The service delivery model used when DAaP is distributed externally via APIs, flat files or cloud platforms
A role responsible for metadata and lineage
questions.explanation: When DAaP is distributed externally it is often exposed as Data-As-a-Service, delivered via APIs, flat files or cloud platforms.

questions.stem: Which of the following is listed as a key trait of Data-As-a-Service (DaaS)?
questions.explanation: DaaS traits include standardised access, SLA-backed reliability and freshness, security controls and throttling, and clear usage agreements and documentation.

questions.stem: In the data product ecosystem, which responsibility belongs to the data steward rather than the Data Product Owner?
options: Defining the DAaP vision and business case
Aligning with platform engineering and business units
questions.explanation: The data steward governs metadata, lineage and compliance, alongside data quality, contract enforcement and versioning support; the other items are DPO responsibilities.

questions.stem: How is the Data Product Owner described within the DAaP ecosystem?
options: The database administrator for the warehouse
An external auditor of data quality
The person who writes the ETL code
The single-threaded leader responsible for the productisation lifecycle
questions.explanation: The Data Product Owner is the single-threaded leader responsible for the productisation lifecycle, acting as product manager of data.
